==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|swop}}{{attn|en|in what circumstances?}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈswɒp/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Mélange a trois-swap.wav|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈswɑp/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-swap.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒp|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|swap}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:swappen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|swappen|t=to swap}}, originally meaning "to hurl" or "to strike", the word alludes to striking hands together when making an exchange; probably from {{inh|en|ang|*swappian}}, a secondary form of {{inh|en|ang|swāpan||to swoop}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|schwappen||to slosh, slop}}. Compare also {{noncog|enm|swippen|t=to strike, hit}}, from {{noncog|ang|swipian|t=to scourge, strike, beat, lash}}, {{noncog|non|svipa|t=to swoop, flash, whip, look after, look around}}. More at {{m|en|swipe}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[exchange#Verb|exchange]] or [[give]] (something) in an non-normal exchange (for something else).
#: {{synonyms|en|exchange|switch|trade}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[hit#Verb|hit]], to [[strike#Verb|strike]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1954|author=C. S. Lewis|title=The Horse and His Boy
|passage="Maybe Apes will grow honest, Sister," said Edmund. "But, by the Lion, if he breaks it again, it may be in such time and place that any of us could '''swap''' off his head in clean battle."}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[beat#Verb|beat]] the [[air#Noun|air]], or [[ply#Verb|ply]] the [[wing#Noun|wings]], with a [[sweeping#Adjective|sweeping]] [[motion]] or [[noise]]; to [[flap#Verb|flap]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[descend]] or [[fall#Verb|fall]]; to [[rush#Verb|rush]] [[hastily]] or [[violently]].
<!--this sense also found in Charles Richardson's "New Dictionary of the English Language" (1836-7)-->

===Etymology 2===
From the verb {{m|en|swap}}. {{etydate|1620}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}
[[File:Swapping apples.svg|thumb| [[w:en:Alice and Bob|Alice]] has a red apple and Bob has a green apple. After a '''swap''', Alice has the green apple and Bob has the red apple.]]

# An [[exchange]] of two comparable things.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1819|author=w:Sir Walter Scott|title=w:Tales of My Landlord|section=The Bride of Lammermoor|passage=I e’en changed it, as occasion served, with the skippers o’ Dutch luggers and French vessels, for gin and brandy{{...}} a gude '''swap''' too, between what cheereth the soul of man and that which dingeth it clean out of his body}}
#* {{RQ:Time|title=Who Is Cilia Flores? What to Know About Maduro’s Wife Amid Fall of Venezuela's First Couple|date=Jan 5 2026|author=Callum Sutherland|text=Flores' nephews were each sentenced to 18 years' imprisonment in 2017 for conspiring to import cocaine, but they were released in 2022 by the Biden Administration as part of a prisoner '''swap''' with Venezuela.|url=https://time.com/7343188/who-is-cilia-flores-maduro-wife-venezuela-politics/|accessdate=6 January 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106103344/https://time.com/7343188/who-is-cilia-flores-maduro-wife-venezuela-politics/|archivedate=6 January 2026}}
# {{lb|en|finance}} A financial [[derivative]] in which two parties agree to exchange one stream of non-normal [[cashflow]] against another stream.
# {{lb|en|computing|informal|uncountable}} Space available in a [[swap file]] for use as [[auxiliary]] [[memory]].
#: {{ux|en|How much '''swap''' do you need?}}
# {{lb|en|Cantab slang}} A social meal at a [[restaurant]] between two [[university]] [[society|societies]], usually involving [[drinking]] and [[banter]]; commonly associated with [[fine|fining]] and [[penny]]ing; equivalent to a [[crewdate]] at {{w|University of Oxford|Oxford University}}.
